  • Also of note is The Sound of Fury's unusual interpretation of Hell, which rather than the usual Biblical/Nordic/Ancient Greek depictions we get in games, is a washed-out mashup of what the Steam page calls "humanity's darkest chapters." Thus, you fight not red-skinned horned imps but gasmasked soldiers and Klu Klux Klansmen, with history-spanning anomalies distorting an otherwise 19th century-flavoured fantasyscape.

Sources indicate that my firstest-ever Golden Joystick Awards, which took place last night in London, was marred somewhat by 1) a gin & tonic costing eleven quid and 2) my view of the stage being directly obscured by its own rigging. Nonetheless, I did crane enough to get a good view at the reveal of The Sound of Fury, a musically-minded hack 'n' slash in which a troubled classical musician descends into Hell to save a friend from the Devil.

Industry observers note that it's not out until late 2027, and the strength of its monster-battering will of course lay in how it feels in the hand. I like the look of this one, though. While it doesn't appear to be a full-on rhythm action game in the Hi-Fi Rush or Dead as Disco vein, it's clearly trying incorporate our glum hero's virtuosity with both visual and thematic flair: spinning attacks are accentuated by trails of sheet music staves, and at least one move inflicts enemies with uncontrollable bouts of dancing. Weapons also take the form of instruments, the trailer being particularly keen to show grand pianos being powerbombed into demon heads. "You dropped your... keys," I will say, to the demons. Heh heh heh.

Also of note is The Sound of Fury's unusual interpretation of Hell, which rather than the usual Biblical/Nordic/Ancient Greek depictions we get in games, is a washed-out mashup of what the Steam page calls "humanity's darkest chapters." Thus, you fight not red-skinned horned imps but gasmasked soldiers and Klu Klux Klansmen, with history-spanning anomalies distorting an otherwise 19th century-flavoured fantasyscape. The laws of time evidently aren't followed here, not least when the protag whips out a Flying V guitar to give the Grim Reaper a different kind of axe wound.

According to recent reports, I can't find much else out about developers and self-publishers Games By Wojtek, with that pluralisation assuming 'they' aren't just one person named Wojtek, but The Sound of Fury looks to be his/their debut game. Hopefully it gets a demo, in due course, so we can try tickling its ivories ourselves.

Battlefield 6's next season will speed up battle pass progression, and make it so Redsec players who don't own the game can actually make progress

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch.
  • Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a newly introduced blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing complications with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.
  • Recent findings suggest that we know that Season 2 is introducing a big new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the new content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a newly introduced blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing complications with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

Recent findings suggest that we know that Season 2 is introducing a big new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

It has been revealed that the real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the latest season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

In a recent development, challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

According to recent reports, BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

It has been revealed that movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

Feature: 20 Wii Exclusives You Should Track Down While You Still Can

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1229 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Somehow, someway, it's been two whole decades since the Revolution began and an elderly relative who had never played a video game in their life somehow, someway, thrashed you at Wii Sports bowling.
  • The little system that could went on to sell over 100 million units across its lifetime, which means that 20 years on it's still possible to pick up a good clean one for a reasonable price - something which can't be remarked for a certain autostereoscopic handheld with a divergent family tree.
  • It also means that secondhand software is still plentiful for the most part, with much of the system's catalogue still available for not-silly money (plus some for silly money).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Somehow, someway, it's been two whole decades since the Revolution began and an elderly relative who had never played a video game in their life somehow, someway, thrashed you at Wii Sports bowling.

The little system that could went on to sell over 100 million units across its lifetime, which means that 20 years on it's still possible to pick up a good clean one for a reasonable price - something which can't be remarked for a certain autostereoscopic handheld with a divergent family tree.

It also means that secondhand software is still plentiful for the most part, with much of the system's catalogue still available for not-silly money (plus some for silly money). So today we're rounding up 20 gems to consider picking up for your trusty Wii.

Sources indicate that if you're just looking for the Best Wii Games™, we've got you covered elsewhere. Here, we're specifically looking for games slightly off the beaten track, games that were either full-on exclusives or, in a couple of cases where I've stretched the definition, are difficult to find anywhere else.

Ready? Let's dive right into things...

Kicking things off with the Batman, Wayforward's take on the Cartoon Network series captured perfectly the audio-visual elements of the show with a ton of amusing dialogue and a fun, animated take on a character that — outside of his Lego iteration — had gotten pretty dark and self-serious in the movies and other games of the era.

Recent findings suggest that batman: The Brave and the Bold - The Videogame (or Das Videospiel as my German copy has it) offers simple side-scrolling brawling, but the BAM-BOOM-POW energy is infectious, and this is a great one to play with the kids. There was a DS version, although that's single-player only, so stick with Wii.

According to recent reports, steven Spielberg's making a game, everybody! Legendary Hollywood director Steven Spielberg! The moment we heard that, we imagined Indiana Jones-style derring-do, or something with aliens or dinosaurs. We didn't imagine that the title prominently flagged as "A Steven Spielberg / EA Game" would be a physics-based block puzzler/party game in the Jenga mould.

However, 2008's Boom Blox turned out to be an absolute blast, especially with friends, and a game that made great use of the system's unique controller. it absolutely deserves to be revisited.

A sequel, Boom Blox Bash Party, followed in 2009, and that's a good time, too.

Dead Space: Extraction was a prequel to the 360-era sci-fi/survival horror game PS3/360 game, and perhaps benefited from low expectations, but it's a cracking, moody little rail shooter.

This one came to PS3 two years later with Move controller support, but this rail shooter was built for the Wii and made use of one of the system's best features: the IR camera-powered pointer in the Wiimotes. For accuracy and responsiveness, this fairly low-tech solution to pointer controls still trumps the gyro alternative (which constantly needs resetting/recentring) in our book, and this game is worth setting up the sensor bar.

One of the few games Europeans got which never saw the light of day in North America, Disaster: Day of Crisis is a Monolith Soft joint that showcases the Wiimote's versatility with different control schemes across its four main gameplay styles, which naturally includes those video game staples, shooting and driving.

The latter is handled with the Remote held horizontally, while outside the Nunchuk-controlled walking sections, the game becomes a pointer-based rail shooter.

With a blockbusting story that crams in volcanoes alongside shady outfits and plenty of (melo)drama, it doesn't quite cohere as it should, and there are certainly better-looking titles on the system. But as a curio from a studio with an enviable pedigree — and a game that apparently didn't pass Reggie Fils-Aimé's quality bar for release — it's a fascinating glimpse at Monolith's Wii-era thinking before Xenoblade Chronicles dropped two years later.

Excite Truck was an underrated gem in the Wii's early life, with satisfying motion controls that paired beautifully with the wallow-y physics of the arcade monster trucks you raced.

It also let you load up MP3s on your SD card and make your own soundtrack, which felt like a bit of magic to some Wii gamers (read: this Wii gamer) back in 2006. Nothing like boosting over a canyon with Gwen Stefani booming through the speakers. Good times.

It has been revealed that having recently fired up Excite Truck, I can confirm that this holds up beautifully, with subtle controls and a suitable sense of heft and face-blasting speed. Helluva game.

Excitebots, Monster Games' 2009 follow-up, kept the arcade sensibilities and challenging terrain but switched out the trucks for on-wheel robots. It's a fantastic game that injects a little more personality into the basic structure of Excite Truck while keeping the speed and excitement.

It has been revealed that sadly, it's also a game which never launched in Europe, so we're currently tit-for-tat after Disaster: Day of Crisis. North America got the better deal, there.

Look, it's an inconsequential Zelda spin-off designed to showcase the Wii Zapper, but it is a system-exclusive inconsequential Zelda spin-off. Can you afford not to have it in your collection?

Hmm, probably. There's a reason this target-practice game is bottom of our Zelda list. Still, it's not unenjoyable, still dirt cheap, and it's got Twilight Princess-era Link on the box. I've somehow ended up with two copies. One of those 'oh, I don't have this' moments when you get home and realise 'yes, I already have this.'.

Another 'built for Wii' game that came to other platforms later (Vita in 2012, PC in 2016), Cing's Little King's Story added dashes of Doshin The Giant and Pikmin to a real-time strategy tale of the titular diminutive king working to expand the reach of his kingdom one citizen at a time and conquer neighbouring territories,.

According to recent reports, an engaging genre mash-up that holds its own alongside the previously mentioned Pikmin series while putting a fresh spin on things, this was one of the last games Cing (Hotel Dusk, Another Code) released. Two years later, the firm filed for bankruptcy.

When PlatinumGames' name is on the box, you expect style - and MadWorld certainly delivered that with its inky, Sin City-esque aesthetic that splattered blood red across a black-and-white canvas.

At a time when all the serious games elsewhere were shiny and brown and grey, this Sega-published chainsaw-'em-up also helped demonstrate that Wii wasn't only a console for fluffy technicolour worlds and cuddly mascots.

In a recent development, as a hack-and-slash brawler, it's not up there with the developer's finest work - there's definitely an element of style over substance here. But when the style is this good, it's still worth the space on the shelf.

It has been revealed that honestly, at this point we all thought we'd have access to this on Switch one way or another — via NSO if not a proper remaster. However, at the time of writing (and discounting the now-unavailable Wii U eShop release of the Trilogy), this Metroid is still a Wii exclusive.

We can only assume it will arrive at some point — Nintendo now has the four Pikmin games on Switch, so it's about time to plug the Prime gap, too.

And staying on that theme, let's stick with Samus over the page...

According to recent reports, since we're already sharing trailers from non-Geoff awards shows, here's another: a first in-motion look at Lola's Familiars: Prison of Argnoh, a 2D side-scroller and "lite-vania" that sees its shy witch-in-training making her first summonable friends. Then, borrowing their powers to bust out of a dark fantasy oubliette.

It looks like this'll be a mix of passively familiar-enhanced punching and more active, mayhaps traditionally Metroid-y power upgrades, Lola's ghastly pals looming over her tiny frame when called upon. It's all presented in a hand-drawn, lightly anime-ish style, complete with a story setup straight out of Saturday morning TV – Lola's only stuck in Skullcatraz because of a summoning-gone-wrong that occurred in pursuit of her school's unlikely Ofsted-compliant 'familiar contest'. I've attended school several times, and will attest that non-sporting contests, which students remain unaware of until seeing a poster for them, do not exist outside of childrens' television*.

In a recent development, this doesn't seem to be kid fodder, though. Lola's a bean but the familiars, and the prison's other denizens, are growling towers of jaws and decaying flesh. Developers Caracal Games are promising they'll star in a "heartfelt and emotionally resonant story about growth," to balance out the grimness, though I'm less clear on a following blurb point that declares it a "lite-vania," into which you'll "dive into exploration, trial-and-error and platforming, without feeling frustrated." While this might just be an attempt to assuage fears that this'll a Hollow Knight- or Nine Sols-style controller-thrower, I do wonder how one goes light on 'vania. Maybe some of the ability gates open if you just ask them nicely?

That aside, I'm already quite charmed by Lola's Familiars, especially the designs of its bag-eyed wallflower of a heroine and her contrastingly hench minions. Release date is TBC, but the Steam page is up.

*Granted, no TV example was ever as egregiously misleading as Jack Black vehicle School of Rock, which convinced me - then a barely-pubescent aspiring bassist - that winning a local Battle of the Bands would pay out thousands in cash, as opposed to the drinks rounds and packs of guitar strings I'd end up competing for a few years later.

  • The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that diablo 4’s segment in the significant Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

It has been revealed that the livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the upcoming class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s latest region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two latest endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Intends lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a fresh activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

In a recent development, echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

Industry observers note that we also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as newly introduced quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

10 Best N64 Racing Games That Still Hold Up Today

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1746 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Let's just get something out of the way quickly – you don't necessarily have to be great at a genre of games to enjoy playing them.
  • Most of the time I spent with racing games was on older consoles, most especially the Nintendo 64.
  • There's a lot of great games here, and so to avoid unnecessary bias, I've ranked them in large part based on their review score aggregates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let's just get something out of the way quickly – you don't necessarily have to be great at a genre of games to enjoy playing them. I mean, sure, I'm quite good at platformers and deckbuilders, and play a ton of those. But if I just stuck with them, I'd get bored eventually. Which is why I enjoy genres I'm not particularly good at, like racing games.

Most of the time I spent with racing games was on older consoles, most especially the Nintendo 64. I clocked tons and tons of hours in many of them back then, and not just the most generic car racing games. I also played snowboarding games, water sports and even futuristic race car rallies. And honestly, every game on this N64 list still holds up today.

There's a lot of great games here, and so to avoid unnecessary bias, I've ranked them in large part based on their review score aggregates. Though in some cases, I did shuffle the order a bit when common sense called for it. So get ready, get set, and let's go through some epic N64 racing games!

In a recent development, nintendo doesn't always have the most luck with launch titles, at least when they're not heavy hitters like Mario or Zelda. Which is why I was so delighted with Pilotwings 64 heralding the new console. It was very stylish, and built on the previous SNES adventure in great ways.

It has been revealed that your goal is to prove your stuff to earn a variety of pilot licenses in the game, and you'll have to accomplish some challenging feats. Those include autogyro, jet pack and hang gliding, even a human cannonball. Feats that aren't for the timid.

Even though the game is graphically less impressive today, the core gameplay still holds up, and offers a robust challenge and plenty of bonus activities for players. And thanks to the hard work Paradigm put in researching military vehicles and flight sims, Pilotwings 64 is just as relevant today as it was back then.

It shows the breadth of the racing game library on the N64 when the first futuristic racer isn't F-Zero X, but instead is Extreme-G. Which isn't a dig, mind you, since both games offered a lot. But for this particular adventure, the highlights were some really epic weapons like homing missiles and laser mines, as well as really innovative, gravity defying courses.

It has been revealed that the game also featured frenetic deathmatches, which made sense on paper, but in execution were a bit muddled. Sure, there's the likes of capture the flag, competitive racing and battle mode, but they were less fun than they were stress inducing.

The biggest reason Extreme-G isn't ranked higher on this list is likely due to the graphics, which were fine but not overly impressive or creative. Still, if you had a need for speed and didn't mind using powerful weapons, this was a thrilling adventure.

Sources indicate that while your mileage with arcade machines may vary, generally speaking they're substantial, bold and visually impressive. And that goes double for racing games like San Francisco Rush 2049. Thankfully, they ported it to the N64, and brought high-octane energy to Nintendo's console.

It has been revealed that what was most impressive about this adventure on consoles is that you could extend wings from your vehicles and glide in mid-air. You'll mostly use that in the stunt mode to rack up crazy points as you do complex maneuvers.

Best of all, you had a lot to unlock in San Francisco Rush 2049, including new cars and tracks. Meaning that even now, this is a racing game you'll be spending a lot of time playing on the Nintendo 64 and even PC.

Industry observers note that since the developer of the Wipeout series was owned by Sony Computer Entertainment, it makes sense most of the games weren't on Nintendo consoles. The one exception was Wipeout 64. While perhaps not a true sequel to Wipeout 2097, this standalone Nintendo adventure offered a lot to enjoy.

It has been revealed that perhaps the most impressive way Wipeout 64 differentiated itself from the others in the series was a split screen allowing up to 4 players to play together. Even with that aside, the game offered robust anti-gravity racing and truly superior track design.

According to recent reports, if you enjoy racers with a variety of weapons, great tracks and a variety of gameplay modes, this N64 game had you covered. That stated, perhaps the graphics were a step down from some of the other entries, but this was still a remarkably fun game.

It has been revealed that much as I love Nintendo, sometimes you have to wait a long while between sequels. Zelda fans know what I'm talking about, but even they didn't have to wait as long for a sequel as fans of the original Excitebike on the NES. 16 years later, it got its first sequel in Excitebike 64.

It has been revealed that as you might expect, the jump from 2D to 3D was a substantial one, and you're capable of epic tricks in Excitebike 64. Brake, slide, turbo boost and even tilt the bike in midair, there's a lot of options. Better yet, the various playable athletes have distinct stats, allowing players to pick the one that works best with their style.

My favorite aspect of the game is playing through the extensive season mode, unlocking fresh content along the way. But the one part of the game that really sets it apart is using the track editor to make your own insane obstacle courses.

According to recent reports, racing games on Nintendo consoles often lean into the fantastical, patterning themselves after the likes of Mario Kart. But one that really took a massive swing was Diddy Kong Racing. Not only did it feature different vehicles ranging from car to hovercraft to aeroplane, but there were also several different drivers and even a story involving the nefarious Wizpig.

Industry observers note that like any of the Donkey Kong games, there's a lot of unlockables here, including obtaining amulet pieces to battle the true final boss. And if that wasn't enough, you'll even deal with actual boss battles of sorts, and use balloons to gain a huge variety of powerups, ranging from missiles to speed boosts and shields.

Industry observers note that best of all, Diddy Kong Racing was quite pretty for the time, and the graphical style still looks great years later. Sure, it could get a bit repetitive, but this was still a really outstanding game you'd need to play on Nintendo 64.

I mentioned earlier that I'm not the best at racing games, but I'm especially bad when they're on water. Which perhaps makes Wave Race 64 especially intimidating. That said, if you put in enough practice time, even a rookie at the genre would find themselves loving this innovative and stunt-filled racing adventure.

In a recent development, playing against the clock while trying to steer your way around buoys and avoid the hazing of your opponent could be really tough. If you're skilled, you'll power up and go even faster, but if you fail, you'll get way behind. Thankfully, though, this is a quite attractive N64 game which is even better when racing against a friend.

It has been revealed that if you're more skilled at racing than me, you'll probably adore Wave Race 64. It's the sort of retro that still holds up today, and it offers a phenomenally fun time, assuming you can react quickly to the choppy waters.

Sources indicate that even though I never played any skateboarding games, I really adored Snowboard Kids. I'm not sure what it was about this N64 adventure, but it hooked me hard. Maybe it was the cute, cartoony graphics, or the simple yet well balanced gameplay. But this was one of those games I found myself playing again and again.

Recent findings suggest that the simple hook of the game is doing tricks while airborne to get coins, and then using them to buy powerups on tracks. You can have active and support items, such as hurling rocks at your opponents or turning temporarily invisible.

According to recent reports, perhaps the most surprising aspect of Snowboard Kids was that it was published by Atlus, who are usually known for JRPGs. But this is just one of those games that is still a ton of fun today, which I can attest to having played it recently with my close friends on their N64.

In a recent development, even though I'm not amazing at racing games, I spent many, many hours playing Mario Kart 64. I barely touched Super Mario Kart, didn't do much with the later entries, but that N64 game was one I kept returning to with friends.

There was just something about this game that made it one of the most iconic entries in the longrunning series. Maybe it was the quirky cast of Mario characters, maybe it was tracks like Rainbow Road. But this was a truly fun racing game that appealed to players of various abilities.

Industry observers note that mix in various engine classes, a wide class of racers and amazingly fun attack items, and you have a great game in Mario Kart 64. But if that wasn't enough, it also features some of the best courses in the series, complete with really catchy tunes.

If you have a need for speed, you need look no further than F-Zero X. This futuristic series featured some of the most blisteringly fast courses and crazy racers you'll see in any series. And honestly, F-Zero X is still probably one of the best racers ever. So even though it's shameful we haven't gotten a sequel, you might not need it either.

According to recent reports, death Race offered a truly unhinged way to play the game, and the randomness of X-Cup could keep you playing the game for a long time. So even though it's not the most graphically impressive game, the high framerate and fantasically weird drivers made this a worthy contender.

It has been revealed that plasma Powered hovercars turned made racing even more fun, and so long as you can keep up, you'll find one of the best racers ever in F-Zero X. Here's hoping it gets an even better followup on modern consoles one day.

#52051. Toy Story 3 Remaster Demonstrates How Movie Games Should Be Done

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (887 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thegamer ↗ Open Full Page

Toy Story 3 Remaster Demonstrates How Movie Games Should Be Done

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (887 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toy Story 3 is often regarded as one of the better games based on a movie.
  • It has been revealed that not only bring those games back, but bundle them together.
  • In a recent development, for decades, movie tie-in games were commonplace.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toy Story 3 is often regarded as one of the better games based on a movie. A legitimately great 3D platformer that also immerses fans of the films in its world in ways that not many other tie-in games have ever managed to pull off. That’s why those of us who played it when it originally released were thrilled to find out it was part of Digital Eclipse’s surprising effort to bring pretty much all past Toy Story games to modern platforms.

It has been revealed that not only bring those games back, but bundle them together. The Retro Roundup, which combines all of the older games from the ‘90s and early ‘00s into one collection, and a remaster of Toy Story 3 for modern platforms. Best of all, the Roundup and the remaster can be bought as part of the same bundle, not just digitally, but physically, too.

In a recent development, for decades, movie tie-in games were commonplace. Almost expected, particularly for the bigger Disney blockbusters. Aladdin, Hercules, Tarzan - they all had games that were released alongside their movies, giving fans another way to experience what they had just seen on the substantial screen.

That tradition has all but died out for several reasons. Trying to release a game and a movie at the same time is no longer possible, largely due to how long it takes to make games that would be considered worthy of big-budget blockbusters. Even if a developer were to hit the ground running the second the mere idea for a movie was uttered, that movie would still end up getting made long before the game was even close to being finished, likely by a margin of years.

Recent findings suggest that it’s why Toy Story 3 was probably one of the last true movie tie-in games we will ever get, which is somewhat ironic as it’s also one of the best. The trouble is, especially now with the release of its remaster, people are looking back on it and longing for another era where movies can have tie-in games released alongside them. It’s not the feeling of long-lost nostalgia we should be focusing on when playing this remaster, though. Developers and movie studios should be looking at what Disney and Avalanche did with that original game, what Digital Eclipse has done with the remaster, and using all of that as the blueprint for the future of movie games.

According to recent reports, even though the Toy Story 3 game and movie were released at the same time, the former isn’t just a game version of the latter. It’s effectively a love letter to the entire series, or at least the original trilogy, that pulls from those first three beloved movies. Its developers were given more freedom, which is how we wound up with the more open Woody’s Roundup area, one of the - if not the - main reasons the game was so popular.

Industry observers note that the game didn’t need to release alongside the movie to be a success, something its Complete Edition has now proved 16 years later. Those who played the original have been reminded of just how good it was, and how it told a separate Toy Story story while remaining faithful to the films, and Disney now has a shiny fresh polished version to point new, younger fans towards not just when a new Toy Story movie is released, but whenever they need to.

In a recent development, that’s the lesson that other studios which have all-but given up on movie games really need to try and learn from. That you don’t need to pull off the almost-impossible and try to get the launch of a movie and its game to perfectly align. What’s more important is making sure that game is good and can stand the test of time. If so, you can not only release it whenever, but whenever you need it again, you have something to point to. Or, if it’s been long enough, you can give it the remaster treatment like Toy Story 3.

I wouldn’t even be averse to seeing Toy Story 3 dusted off and remastered a second time a decade from now, perhaps to give Toy Story fans who haven’t even been born yet something to play two console generations from now when the sixth, seventh, and eighth movies are released. Add an extra area to Woody’s Roundup. Throw in a few more story missions. It’s certainly a lot easier than making a whole new game from scratch, which is the problem that has effectively ended the movie video game era.

In a recent development, I appreciate that “Hey, just make a game that’s as good as Toy Story 3 and you’ll be set for life” is easier said than done. The thing is, I don’t think anyone is even trying. Just look at the excitement surrounding the reveal of the Coco world in Kingdom Hearts 4. There’s a Coco sequel coming, and a game like Toy Story 3 set in that world could be huge, even if it doesn’t line up with the release of its sequel. Sadly, I think Coco’s inclusion in KH is the closest we’ll ever get to a video game set in Disney’s Land of the Dead.

  • Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game.
  • As his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm.
  • Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

As his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:.

Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

Industry observers note that cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” notes game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

Recent findings suggest that in addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Mega Man: Dual Override releases in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

Conan: The Black Pyramid shoves the titular barbarian into a very Hades-inspired action roguelite with the addition of a few other familiar heroes

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game.
  • According to recent reports, conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more!
  • Where it is similar to Hades lies in the fact that the titular triangle changes in form each time you go in it, and of course there are different abilities and buffs to pick up along the way to aid you in your quest.

I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game. Obviously there are plenty of genres that are trendy to imitate, but how often do you see something that's just sort of "thing you know slapped on top of game you know?" Perhaps that's a tad mean, but I do genuinely have a fondness for such games, so I'm quite pleased by the announcement of Conan: The Black Pyramid, an action roguelite RPG that so clearly went to Supergiant Games' School of Hades you have to admire the boldness just a little bit.

According to recent reports, conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more! So, immediately, a notable enough difference from Hades, and one that seems like a neat take. As one of them you then "Descend into eldritch chambers of the Black Pyramid, a mysterious and dangerous place that defies the logic of space and time. Confront the shadows of the champions themselves and piece together the dark secrets of their past.".

Where it is similar to Hades lies in the fact that the titular triangle changes in form each time you go in it, and of course there are different abilities and buffs to pick up along the way to aid you in your quest. Each character has their own combination of weapons and abilities, so it does sound like you can mix it up quite nicely. There is, also, 2-player online co-op (sorry to the couch lovers, I suppose), adding to the ways it differs and making it a tad more friendly for those that have exactly one friend who also loves Conan.

Overall, seems like a fresh enough take on Hades while still trying to find some amount of its own identity. And hey, Hades is great, so I'm never upset about having a little bit more of that kind of game. No release date attached to Conan: The Black Pyramid just yet, but it is planned to arrive sometime in 2027. You can check it out on Steam here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love.
  • As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

Sources indicate that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be confirmed tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

In a recent development, last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest upgrade, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for upgrade 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an concern that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s upgrade takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an matter that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

According to recent reports, look at you, you lucky devil, you're being treated to a upcoming Warhammer 40,000: Darktide class next month! This class is called the Sisters Novitiate, a group of wonderfully violent women with a penchant for crossbows, burning people alive and putting a stop to anyone that dares to oppose the God-Emperor. Neato!

According to a blog post accompanying the reveal of the class, the Sisters Novitiate work a tad differently compared to other classes available in the game. "Unlike other classes, the Sisters Novitiate are able to choose from six divine and devastating Acts of Faith, as opposed to blitz and combat abilities," the post explains. "Their abilities draw upon reserves of Faith, allowing them to unleash brutal Neural Whip attacks to the inspiring Icon of Purity and protective prayers. Faith can take many forms for the Sisters Novitiate, each channeling the Emperor's divine will and bringing his wrath upon his enemies.".

It has been revealed that you build up their Faith while fighting, in turn choosing from a selection of doctrines and pledges in their talent tree, "each shaping how Faith is both accumulated and put to use. Any two Acts of Faith can be equipped at a time, allowing players to choose how their Novitiate will unleash righteous fury on the battlefield." I mentioned crossbows, right? Well, I stand lore corrected, as what they technically have is the Condemnor Stakethrower, which "pins what remains of their enemies to the walls." They do also have access to a flamethrower, a significant ole mace, your classic sword and shield, and whatever the hell a "Penitent Eviscerator.".

Industry observers note that this DLC class also comes the same day as a free update, which will introduce the Metlagun, equipable by the Sisters Novitiate as well as the Veteran. Apparently there'll be more information on the free update soon. Oh, and the release date! It's December 7th, so a little under a month away. I'm sure you can (Dark)tide over the next few weeks by rewatching the gnarly reveal trailer.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Titled the Criminal Profile, both Jason and Lucia have distinct mental and social states based on how they handle their criminal and civilian lives around Leonida.
  • Grand Theft Auto 6’s Criminal Profiles are split into 5 different categories, with 4 that you can freely move between over the course of the game with little consequence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6 has pulled plenty of mechanics from previous Rockstar titles, mostly focusing on revamping systems from previous GTA titles to make them feel incredibly in-depth. Even with this clear focus, some standout parts of other Rockstar titles have made the jump, including a revamp of Red Dead Redemption’s Honor System.

Titled the Criminal Profile, both Jason and Lucia have distinct mental and social states based on how they handle their criminal and civilian lives around Leonida. More so than Honor, the Criminal Profile affects various story moments, the game’s ending, and central mechanic functions from fight to fight. Let’s go over all 5 distinct states, what they offer, and how to ensure your Criminal Profile stays consistent.

Grand Theft Auto 6’s Criminal Profiles are split into 5 different categories, with 4 that you can freely move between over the course of the game with little consequence. These 5 tiers include Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable.

According to recent reports, the profiles split down the middle: Professional and Hardened lean toward more controlled, non-lethal play, while Violent and Psycho reward wild aggression and quick thinking. Depending on your Criminal Profile, Jason and Lucia will act differently both toward each other and the events of the story.

Leaning one way on the scale or the other will also alter how you regain Focus in combat, allowing you to more accurately land shots and handle threats.

Professional and Hardened characters regain extra Focus via nonlethal gun takedowns, knockouts, and stealth takedowns.

Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable characters gain boosts of Focus while landing headshots, lethal takedowns, or finishing off downed opponents.

Either way, your Criminal Profile rewards you for leaning into the identity of the profile, with extra Focus gain if you’re further along the scale (Professional or Psycho/Irredeemable).

In a recent development, your Criminal Profiles are also a major factor in your eventual ending, heavily altering how Jason and Lucia act during major story events. In short, play how you want Lucia and Jason to act, either as professionals with an outer goal in mind, or as menaces who love the chaos they cause.

Irredeemable is an outlier, as there is no way to leave it once you achieve it. As the name implies, becoming Irredeemable requires repeated acts of incredible, heinous violence for the sake of it. An Irredeemable Criminal Profile is deliberately impossible to achieve by accident, as you’re given repeated warnings and chances to bring yourself back.

According to recent reports, to earn each different Criminal Profile, you’ll need to play in the ways that each profile rewards, making the process of earning and benefiting from the profiles rather natural. For example, if you want to be seen as a Professional, play professionally. If you want to be a Psycho, walk around Leonida lashing out and kicking puppies, you sicko.

Taking on drug dens, robberies, and optional missions is a great way to earn points either way, especially if you want to correct your Criminal Profile before you continue the main story.

Rob Run Is Surging On Steam As PC Players Look For A GTA 6 Alternative

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that rockstar still hasn't confirmed when GTA 6 will launch on PC, and judging by past releases, it could take anywhere from 7 to 19 months.
  • Industry observers note that rob Run, a cops-and-robbers "crime sandbox" where every single cop and robber is played by a "living breathing human," debuted on Steam earlier this month.
  • On November 15, Rob Run hit a peak of over half-a-million players with a 549,661 CCU, and has continued to hold firm while PC players watch from the sidelines as every single social media feed is flooded with posts about GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that rockstar still hasn't confirmed when GTA 6 will launch on PC, and judging by past releases, it could take anywhere from 7 to 19 months. However, one game is already filling the void.

Industry observers note that rob Run, a cops-and-robbers "crime sandbox" where every single cop and robber is played by a "living breathing human," debuted on Steam earlier this month. It was a pretty successful release for Last Day on Earth and Frostborn developer Kefir, with a 23,000 peak on November 4 rising to 43,000 within just a few days — a number that only skyrocketed as GTA 6 got closer and closer.

On November 15, Rob Run hit a peak of over half-a-million players with a 549,661 CCU, and has continued to hold firm while PC players watch from the sidelines as every single social media feed is flooded with posts about GTA 6.

To put those numbers into perspective, it's the fourth most-played game on the platform right now, competing with heavy-hitters like CS2 and Apex Legends:.

It has been revealed that admittedly, Rob Run is closer to something like GTA Online (specifically, RP) than GTA 6, but it has all the hallmarks: bank robberies, police chases, convenience store stick-ups, and the rags-to-riches criminal enterprise story that defines so many Grand Theft Auto games. "In just one week, you can go from being a regular thug to the boss of the server's largest organization," the description reads. "And then start over — with newly introduced experience, allies, and a more ambitious initiative to seize power.".

Industry observers note that it sounds like a solid alternative to GTA 6 on paper, even if it doesn't quite measure up to the charm of NotGTAV, the Snake-like parody where you drive around in a Tesco car park that kept us going while we waited for Los Santos, but there's a big asterisk here. Developer Kefir admits to using AI "in the creation of certain graphic elements," and the 'Mixed' reviews paint a stark picture of cheaters running rampant and a completely unwelcoming community that have made the game impenetrable for newcomers.

"Half enjoyable AI slop rendered completely unplayable due to the worst cheating crisis I've seen since Counter-Strike," reads one review.

"Great concept, ruined by the community," states another. "Cops just kill on sight (KOS) the moment they see you wearing a mask. Criminals aren't any better. Both sides constantly camp selling areas and extraction points, making it almost pointless to even try playing the game as intended.".

"Every store you try to rob is already robbed or you get shot by another player just getting out of your car," warns one reviewer. "Tried to live an honest life and play as a cop but everyone is already playing as a cop so it will not let you. As a latest player, all I could do is drive around and return to Lenny's cause any time I slowed down I got rammed by some other robber.".

Plenty of reviews raise eyebrows that AI appears to have been used more than the disclosure lets on, while complaining of connection issues and long maintenance windows interrupting the experience. Kefir is already working to address some of these problems, adding a more overt report button, improving servers, and limiting voice chat to target toxicity, while also adding more methods to detect cheaters, but the negative reviews only continue to pour in.

Recent findings suggest that "I've never experienced this many hackers in a game before," a review from earlier today claimed. "Within 30 minutes of a server going live, people are already using aimbot and pulling bank heists. Servers not being region locked makes things even worse. The game is also practically unplayable for solo players. Winning a 1v2 is possible, but a 1v3 is impossible [...] The game is fun and has potential, but between hackers, camping, and the huge advantage groups have over solo players, it's honestly more frustrating than enjoyable. Not worth the headache in its current state.".

So, while it might be a solid free-to-play alternative to GTA 6 right now, the reality of Rob Run is a game plagued by overt AI use, cheaters, and a KOS problem that makes DayZ look tame.
